title: Paper Cut
description: Freight paperwork is full of commas — "Port of Los Angeles, CA, USA" is one field, not three. A CSV import that mishandles quoting turns one clean shipment into a garbled reject. Prove the import UI handles it correctly end to end.
successCondition: Uploading a CSV whose originLabel and destinationLabel fields are quoted strings containing commas (e.g. "Port of Los Angeles, CA, USA") alongside otherwise-valid columns results in the CSV import report showing that row as accepted (counted in the Accepted stat tile, not listed among the rejected-row list items), and the newly created shipment subsequently appears on the Tracking dashboard with the full comma-containing label intact, not truncated at the first comma.
hints: Required columns are documented in docs/api/admin.md — quote any field containing a comma per standard CSV rules.
Check the label rendered on /tracking afterward, not just the import report — a parsing bug could still accept the row while corrupting the label.
